projects.title: Nutrivision: A MetaQuest AR/VR Application to Count Calories
projects.description: Presented at Stanford Tree Hacks '25.NutriVision is an AI-powered nutrition tracking tool designed to (1) automatically detect food in real-time using VR/AR glasses and (2) provide accurate calorie and macronutrient analysis to help users effortlessly track their intake. Built on a Flask backend and a React Native frontend, with integrations with YOLOv11 for object detection, OpenAI API for calorie estimation, and USDA Food Database for enhanced nutrient accuracy. The model is deployed using onnxruntime JS to run efficiently on Meta Quest 2, leveraging the live video feed for real-time predictions. PostgreSQL is used for database management to log user consumption trends over time.

projects.title: NeoHb Medical Device: An Embedded Systems Project
projects.description: - Developed a compact, wrist-worn device for non-invasive health monitoring.- Used AT-Mega 328 microcontroller and peripheral hardware components such as photodiode array to collect hemoglobin data noninvasively. - Used a peripheral bluetooth hardware module to continuously send over complex THx spectral data to an Android app, which used SQL database and multithreaded algorithms to store and display spectral data to the app’s UI.- Personally invited to present this work to esteemed figures including the Governor of Massachusetts, President of MIT, and the acclaimed Dr. Anthony Fauci, highlighting the project's significant impact and potential in the field of medical technology.

This is my official goodbye to being the internet's list girl. It's been a crazy journey spending the last two years convincing anyone who would give me two seconds of their day to listen to a pitch about making lists. Deciding to step away from building a product I personally loved so much wasn't easy but undoubtedly was the right thing to do. As you might have seen, both Conner and I are no longer actively working on Ditto . Unfortunately, after countless experiments and iterations, we came to the understanding that the ceiling this specific product was not large enough to allow us to reach the sheer impact and scale that we hope to achieve in building this company. But don't worry, the app itself is still being maintained, it's still available to download if someone resonates with the concept. Also because thousands of people would literally crash out if we removed the app. I will always be grateful for our fiercely loyal users. So what have we been doing the last few months then? Conner, myself and our incredible team (both new and old!) have been relentlessly working on a brand new app around the thesis of unlocking the stories from your camera roll. The camera roll is an untapped dataset representing the most accurate, high‑resolution archive of your life — every phase, friendship, and micro‑era in one place, captured and framed exactly how you saw that moment. Our vision was always much bigger than a form factor. My personal motivation stems from an unwavering belief that it's our job to make the internet a more participatory place. How can it be that our only options to engage with the social products is to lurk and doomscroll, become a full-blown content creator or quit it all together. It's clear that the gap for a new social space could not be wider, more obvious, and more important to get right. I'm super excited to introduce you to our new company Beam Camera Roll but for now, felt like I owed my list girl persona a proper goodbye. I'm also very grateful to have the support of our core team, investors and advisors onboard this new journey with us. So much to come. See ya very soon.

We’re excited to share that Truli is backed by a16z speedrun . Michael and I started Truli after navigating regulatory compliance for our own supplement. What should have been a straightforward process became hours of digging through FDA regulations, guidance documents, and constantly evolving requirements. As we spoke with other CPG founders, we realized this was an industry-wide problem. Today, the stakes are even higher. Functional ingredients, peptides, GLP-1 products, retailer policies, and increasing scrutiny around product claims are making compliance more complex every year. Yet most teams still rely on manual reviews, disconnected tools, and expensive lawyers or consultants. That’s why we’re building Truli: an AI-native compliance platform that helps food, beverage, and supplement companies stay compliant across the entire product lifecycle. We’re working with leading global CPG brands to modernize compliance, making it an invisible layer that enables innovation rather than a bottleneck that slows it down. We’re incredibly grateful to the entire a16z Speedrun team for believing in our vision. Thank you to Jonathan Lai , Fareed Mosavat , Andrew Chen , Joshua Lu , Kenan Saleh , Marcus Segal , Troy Kirwin , Emily Bennett , Seeam Shahid Noor , Samira Behrouzan , Macy Mills , Lester Chen , Tom Hammer , Lejla Johnsen , Andrew Lee , Jordan Mazer , Jordan Carver , Bella Nazzari , Joe G. , Jacqueline Young , Marigold Vu , and Joan DeGennaro for all of their support. We’re also deeply grateful to every customer, advisor, and regulatory expert who has helped shape what we’re building. If you’re navigating compliance in food, beverage, or supplements, we’d love to chat. We’re just getting started.

On a recent summer Sunday afternoon, Brooks Hiller was hunkered over his laptop at his apartment in Chicago, dialing in to hour three of a marathon series of conference calls on real-estate deals. The 21-year-old isn’t a professional, and he doesn’t make a dime from this work. He is a rising senior at Indiana University’s Kelley School of Business, where he leads a team of 20 undergraduates who manage about $12 million in equity. Those students operate their own real-estate investment business, called Sample Gates Management, named for the Gothic-style limestone arches that are the gateway to the Bloomington campus. Unlike the many student investment clubs that deploy university money or rely on donations, the Indiana group raises funds from third parties and invests in properties across the country, such as apartment developments and industrial parks. “Students get the experience, the school gets a better education for their students, and the investors are making their money back and get to be a part of the program again,” Hiller said. “I really wanted to be part of that.” The group’s success is emblematic of changes transforming both higher education and the real-estate industry. 🔗 Read more: https://on.wsj.com/45apwJZ

A few weeks ago, I had the opportunity to present our research poster at the EMERGE Conference, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay Our paper, "Beyond the Turing Test: Assessing the Authenticity of AI-Generated Qualitative Data in HCI," co-authored with Navaneeth Sankar K P , Madhura Regundwar , Taashvi Singh ,and Tanisha Harlalka , explores a question that is becoming increasingly relevant as AI finds its way into the design process: Can AI-generated interview responses ever be considered a substitute for real user research? As designers increasingly use LLMs as "synthetic users" for ideation and qualitative research, understanding where AI aligns with and diverges from authentic human experiences becomes critical. Our research explores these boundaries and the implications they have for human-centered design. It was a great experience presenting our work, learning from the incredible research showcased at the conference, and having thoughtful conversations with fellow researchers. Happy to share that this paper has been selected for the first round of ICoRD. Looking forward to seeing where this research goes next! #HCI #UXResearch #ArtificialIntelligence #HumanCenteredDesign #Research #EMERGE #IITBombay
